availability: No reviewed source in the inspected set reports a marketed-availability measure for any London area; Savills 'supply' and vacancy rates are distinct definitions and cannot substitute.
midtown_fringe: Midtown itself remains unmeasured; only City Fringe vacancy history (Q3-Q4 2025) is retained, and City Fringe is not Midtown.
wider_london: Only selected districts (Hammersmith, VNEB, Stratford, Lambeth) are covered; these samples do not represent all wider London.

claims.text: Semafor (published 9 Oct 2026) reports Canary Wharf Group stating office occupancy now exceeds 92% and that it is reporting the highest rental rates in its history; these are owner-reported figures, not an independent area index.
claims.headline: Canary Wharf owner reports 92%+ occupancy

claims.text: Semafor (9 Oct 2026) reports Visa recently leased 300,000 sq ft, Barclays bought its headquarters for £750m, and Citi is investing over $1bn in its European HQ; JPMorgan's 265m tower remains a proposal pending approval.
claims.headline: Canary Wharf tenant commitments reported

claims.text: Reuters-sourced reporting (Cyprus Mail, 5 Oct 2026) says developer LS Estates is sounding out defence and AI occupiers for a refurbished nine-floor Canary Wharf office formerly used by Credit Suisse support staff.
claims.headline: Canary Wharf refurbishment retargeted

claims.text: The same 5 Oct 2026 report states the £100m-plus refit of 17 Columbus Courtyard, backed by GIC and Oaktree, was originally aimed at life sciences with up to 60% of space earmarked for laboratories, but short-term interest from that sector was lower than expected.
claims.headline: Lab-led refit sees weaker life-science interest

claims.text: Knight Frank commentary (published 7 Oct 2026) states London office development activity is not keeping pace with occupier demand for the type of space now required, citing viability pressures and macroeconomic caution.
claims.headline: Knight Frank flags development shortfall

claims.text: London Fire Brigade (published 6 Oct 2026) says Lambeth Council granted planning permission to refurbish its historic Albert Embankment headquarters to provide a fire station, office space and community spaces.
claims.headline: Lambeth HQ refurbishment consented

claims.text: Morgan McKinley's London Employment Monitor (retrieved 10 Oct 2026) reports professional job vacancies in London fell to 4,368 in Q3 2026, down 6% quarter-on-quarter and 11% year-on-year.
claims.headline: London professional vacancies fall in Q3

claims.text: The same monitor reports monthly professional vacancies fell from 1,719 in July to 1,449 in August and 1,200 in September 2026, a 30% decline across the quarter.
claims.headline: Monthly vacancy decline steepens

claims.text: Bank of England (published 17 Sep 2026) held Bank Rate at 3.75% on 16 September 2026 by a 6-3 majority, with three members voting for 4.00%; this is a UK-wide policy rate, not a London office financing cost.
claims.headline: Bank Rate held at 3.75%

claims.text: Bank of England (17 Sep 2026) reports UK CPI inflation rose to 3.1% in August 2026.
claims.headline: UK CPI at 3.1% in August

claims.text: The Bank of England (17 Sep 2026) states UK CPI inflation is likely to rise further over coming quarters; this is a source forecast, not an observed outcome.
claims.headline: BoE expects inflation to rise further

claims.text: ONS (published 15 Sep 2026) reports London's seasonally adjusted employment rate at 73.9% and economic inactivity rate at 20.5% for residents aged 16-64, and unemployment at 6.8% for economically active residents aged 16+, for May-July 2026.
claims.headline: London LFS rates, May-July 2026

claims.text: GLA Economics (retrieved 10 Oct 2026) notes the most recent ONS release showed London real GVA grew 0.3% in 2023 versus 0.4% for the UK, and estimates 1.1% growth in 2024 and 1.9% in 2025.
claims.headline: London GVA: observed 2023, estimated 2024-25

claims.text: GLA Economics (retrieved 10 Oct 2026) cites an official London unemployment rate of 7.4% in March 2026 and attributes recent involuntary worklessness mainly to weaker labour-market demand.
claims.headline: GLA cites 7.4% London unemployment

claims.text: Lendlease (published 8 Jan 2025) describes the Turing Building at Stratford Cross as 350,000 sq ft of Grade A office space, the first building delivered in its joint venture with CPP Investments; completion date and unlet area are not established.
claims.headline: Turing Building, Stratford Cross

claims.text: Lendlease (published 20 Aug 2026) reports plans submitted to Newham Council for the final phase of Stratford Cross, delivering approximately 2,000 homes plus a public park and retail space; a submitted residential-led proposal, not consented office supply.
claims.headline: Stratford Cross final phase submitted

claims.text: Landlord implication: with H1 2026 starts at 1.5m sq ft and mostly refurbishments, and Knight Frank reporting development lagging occupier demand, competition for scarce new and best-quality space may persist; this is interpretation, not a measured outcome.
claims.headline: Scarce new supply may support quality space

claims.text: Landlord implication: the 17 Columbus Courtyard retargeting from life sciences to defence and AI suggests refurbishment strategies may need flexible repositioning when sector demand shifts; interpretation, not a measured market shift.
claims.headline: Refurbishment repositioning risk

claims.text: Watch whether Canary Wharf Group's reported 92%+ occupancy and record rents are corroborated by independent area-level vacancy or rent series, and whether the JPMorgan tower proposal receives approval.
claims.headline: Watch Canary Wharf corroboration

claims.text: Watch whether the reported 30% quarterly fall in London professional vacancies persists into Q4 2026 and whether it feeds through to occupier space requirements.
claims.headline: Watch labour-demand weakness

limitations: No reviewed source in the inspected set provides a marketed-availability measure, so availability is reported as a topic gap rather than inferred from Savills 'supply' or vacancy rates.
Savills 'supply' totals and the Q2 narrative change differ (0.4m vs 0.5m sq ft); rounded source totals are retained and the discrepancy is flagged rather than reconciled.
Prime and Grade A rent passages carry different averaging windows (H1 January-June, January-May YTD, unspecified quarterly); they are not compared as a trend.
Canary Wharf occupancy and record-rent statements are owner-reported via secondary reporting and are not independently verified area metrics.
ONS London labour-market figures are residence-based and cover residents aged 16-64 (employment, inactivity) or 16+ (unemployment); they are not London office employment.
Morgan McKinley's London Employment Monitor is a candidate source pending monitoring validation of its definitions and measurements.
No weekly London office measurement exists in the inspected evidence; no week-over-week comparison is made.
